messages:
maya: quick heads-up — we merged the prefix-merge + eviction-policy update to canary today. early numbers look promising: p50 latency dropped ~35% on short-context traffic and token cost down ~12% on the canary pool. rolling to 10% now.

jon: awesome — is that across g4/g5 or just one instance type?

maya: canary is on g5 for now. we saw the biggest delta on 1-3 token prompts (service p50 went from ~46ms -> ~30ms). long seqs unchanged.

priya: where can I see the perf dashboard and the exact config? want to sanity-check the eval jobs before wider rollout.

maya: dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/1234 (canary metrics + diff). config snippet below:

```
{
  "runtime": {
    "prefix_merge": "enabled",
    "evict_policy": "age_plus_score",
    "kv_max_bytes": "524288",
    "merge_threshold_ms": "15"
  }
}
```

maya: also added a safety fallback: if p95 latency rises >20% for 5min we auto-disable merge for that node and route to baseline.

infra-bot: canary-deploy 1965001234: applied to pool g5-canary-3 — 10% traffic. health checks: OK. p50: -35%, p95: +2%.

jon: nice. any impact on cache hit read amplification or memory pressure?

maya: we did see a small uptick in KV lookups (~3%) due to merging logic, but net token CPU decreased. memory steady; we raised kv_max_bytes for canary so no evictions spiking.

priya: can you paste the smoke eval results? esp. hallucination/regression numbers.

maya: quick paste from smoke: generation-chunked-regression: 0.2% worse, rerank-stability: unchanged, enduser-quality (small prompt set): +0.4% BLEU-ish proxy. overall quality delta within our CI tolerances.

simon: :tada: amazing win. when do we schedule the broader rollout?

maya: aim to 30% by EOD Wed if canary holds for 24h. will open a release-note and a feature flag toggle in the console. tagging @product for awareness.

jon: thanks @maya — lmks if you want a quick postmortem doc or short blurb for eng-all-hands.

maya: will do a short note with graphs tomorrow. thanks all.
